steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (205 degrees C). Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line cups with paper liners.
Whisk milk and lemon juice together in a jug to make sour milk; whisk in eggs and oil until smooth.
Stir flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt together in a large bowl, making a well in the center; pour milk mixture into well and stir just until batter is combined; fold in cranberries.
Spoon batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each 2/3 full; sprinkle with almonds.
Bake in the preheated oven until tops spring back when lightly pressed, about 18 to 20 minutes. Cool in the tin for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Cranberry Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These cranberry muffins with lemon are deliciously sweet and tart. Toasted slivered almonds lend texture to these tender and fluffy treats.

review.reviewBody: These are excellent, fluffy, tasty muffins!! I followed the recipe exactly. Next time I make them I'm going to add some lemon zest cause I LOVE LEMON!! lol! I will now sit down, put my feet up and enjoy 1 (or 2) with a nice cuppa tea :) Thanks for the recipe!!

I made additions but I do this for all recipes I want lemony tang so I'm sharing my tip. I replaced milk with buttermilk then added 2 tsp corn starch to the flour, 2 tsp zest, 1/2 tsp lemon extract and let batter rest 30-60 minutes before filling tins. Whether it's lemon blueberry muffins, these or a fruit pie like apple or cherry...I always add per single batch 2 Tbl of Country Time lemonade! It's the acid I guess but it gives tang that i'll never get with zest or extract yet doesn't change my liquid requirement. I'd tried a muffin recipe that called for the corn starch and the rest time and was Amazed at the delightful fluff it added to the muffins without any gummy worries. One more tip? I also add to my apple pie apples a packet of hot apple cider mix. Alpine is the brand @ Walmart. Does Not throw the sweetness off a bit. I used crumble topping so I baked 8 minutes at 400 then without opening the oven door turned the oven to 350 until they were done. this sets the crumble so it stays put when I take them to a party.

Made these this morning, with a few modifications. This was my second attempt today for lemon blueberry muffins. Used my standard recipe first with modifications, consistency was good but not lemony enough. I found this recipe, and decided to give it a try. 
I used 1/2 cup lemon juice with 1/2 cup milk plus ~1 tsp fresh zest since reviews said lemon flavor was mild. Reduced sugar to 2 cups and added 1/2 cup flour because batter was somwhat thin and I wanted my blueberries suspended. Made mini muffins, 13 min on 380 convection baked nicely, but the muffins were very soft and stuck to pan pretty badly. The lemon flavor was perfect with 1/2 cup lemon juice, strong but not overpowering.
I might try again with this recipe, further modifying to reduce the moisture and sugar and add another 1/2 cup flour, and I would definitely use papers. I'm not a fan of papers normally, but these stuck badly.

Doubled the recipe and added zest from one lemon. Used frozen defrosted whole cranberries and toasted chopped almonds on the stovetop in butter and oil and white and brown sugar. Didn't make enough to top all so sprinkled others with white sugar. Also made some mini loaves and mini muffins since I only have one regular-size muffin tin. These were excellent!

I changed it up so it suited my lifestyle. I switch the flour to all purpose gluten free, added an extra 1/2 tablespoon of baking powder, and change sugar to Stevia substitute, and coconut oil instead of vegetable oil. I also did a brown sugar and crushed almond crumble topping. They are a bit dry si next batch will add a touch more oil and not cook quite as long. They are stillvery tasty and way less calories.

Delicious! I added 2 tablespoons of lemon zest as others had suggested and it gave the muffins a nice subtle background flavor. I also added 1/4 cup of shredded coconut which is a nice touch of chewiness to the muffins. The muffins remained rather pale although they were thoroughly cooked. Next time I plan to increase oven to 420F. Will make these again.

They are tasty muffins! I used oat milk instead of cow’s milk. I added only 1 cup of sugar, and the zest and juice of one full lemon and sprinkled a tiny bit of sugar on the top of each muffin before baking. I also used frozen cranberries so I didn’t cut them in half. They turned out great!

These are quite nice - my modifications include using melted butter instead of oil (used less salt), add 1/4 tsp lemon extract and the zest of one lemon, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract, cut sugar to 1 cup, used craisins that had been softened in hot water, and didn't top with the almonds. I doubled the recipe for 12 jumbo muffins. They freeze well. Thanks for the recipe!

This recipe turned out really nice. I found the lemon flavor a subtle compliment to the cranberries. I followed the recipe closely, adding lemon zest, adjusted the sugar to just over 1 cup and subbed 1/4 wheat flour for white in an attempt to convince myself it was healthy! I also pulsed the cranberries in a processor so they were coarsely chopped & distributed throughout. Will definitely be making again with orange.

Wow Yum! I left out the other 1/4 cup of sugar and added lemon zest because I like it more lemony and less sweet. I used real cranberries and it was great.
I also made it as a loaf instead of muffins, you bake it at 350 uncovered for exactly 1hr and it's perfect.
Saving this recipe.

Very tasty, but they don't have a big lemon taste because of the tartness of the cranberries, I added 1 1/4 c of cranberries. I also added 1 tsp of almond extract (because I had no almonds). I also sprinkled some sparkling sugar on top just before popping these beauties in the oven. They were ready in 20 minutes flat. Muffins were moist and had a slight crispy top like all respected muffins should. Delicious! Thanks for the recipe!
Switched out for df gf ingredients and added a lemon glaze! Turned out awesome!
Turned out very nicely. Will add lemon zest and increase lemon juice next time.
Loved the flavour. Used lemon yogurt to make up some of the liquid required. It needed more time in the oven though I do like slightly large muffin tops.
No changes, just as written, Deliscious! Thank you.
Cathy Stanfield, I put the meon zest in there! OMG they are awesome!!!!

Very good and easy. The only change I made was to add some lemon zest. They didn’t rise a lot but they were light and fluffy. I found they tasted better the second day. Using regular muffin cups, I ended up with 18 muffins, not 12 like the recipe says.
Taste was good, but they sunk in the middle and looked awful. Followed recipe exactly.
Only change was that I used shortening instead of oil since I didn’t have oil- but I still used the same measured amount as if it were the oil and it still tasted delicious 🤤
